title: Capacity hedging and autoscaler regression retrospective
creator: Nora Kim
description: Summary: During a multi-region traffic spike on 2025-08-12 we observed a persistent headroom deficit in several Dedicated pools. Requests experienced elevated tail latency and increased 429 drops despite apparently healthy GPU allocation. This ticket captures the rapid-response mitigations, root-cause analysis, and an action plan to prevent recurrence. Key findings: a recent kernel-selection heuristic change regressed placement decisions for short-sequence chat workloads, causing increased per-instance memory pressure and triggering conservative autoscaler backoffs; autoscaler logic did not account for KV-cache churn leading to underprovisioning during bursty patterns; telemetry lacked a concise headroom signal correlated with latency percentiles.
timeline_notes: 2025-08-12 03:20 UTC: First elevated 95th/99th latency alerts from US-West dedicated pools
2025-08-12 03:40 UTC: Incident commander convened; initial mitigation attempted via emergency routing to overflow pools (partial relief)
2025-08-12 04:05 UTC: Canary rollback of kernel-selection change deployed to restore prior allocation behavior
2025-08-12 05:00 UTC: Autoscaler override applied to force temporary headroom reservation (+20%) for affected pools
2025-08-12 09:30 UTC: Traffic normalized; incident declared mitigated after 4.5 hours
2025-08-13 — 2025-08-30: Forensics and simulation runs to reproduce regression and validate mitigations
root_cause: A heuristic change in the kernel selection layer prioritized memory-frugal kernels for short sequences. For certain chat workloads this increased per-request KV-cache churn and reduced effective throughput per instance. The autoscaler uses CPU/GPU utilization and instance count signals but did not incorporate a cache-warmth or headroom metric, so it interpreted degraded effective throughput as transient and scaled conservatively. Combined with rollout of the heuristic across regions, multiple pools hit a headroom cliff nearly simultaneously.
short_term_mitigations: Rollback kernel-selection heuristic to previous stable variant (rolled within 45 minutes)
Apply emergency autoscaler override to reserve explicit capacity (+20%) for 6 hours per affected pool
Route high-QPS customers to non-impacted overflow pools and enable staggered drain for affected nodes
Increase alerting sensitivity on headroom proxy metric (ad-hoc) to catch reappearance
long_term_action_items: Implement a headroom signal (headroom = available_token_capacity / target_throughput) surfaced to autoscaler and SLO dashboards — owner: Priya Rao — due 2025-10-01
Enhance autoscaler to consume cache-warmth and sequence-profile signals so scaling decisions reflect effective throughput — owner: Diego Alvarez — due 2025-11-15
Introduce pre-merge autoscaler simulation harness that replays production trace for any autoscaler change (simulation pass required for rollout) — owner: Luca Reynolds — due 2025-12-01
Add canary gating for runtime kernel heuristics with traffic-fraction and headroom safeties (automatic rollback if headroom drops >10%) — owner: Asha Patel — due 2025-10-20
Create a capacity hedging policy (configurable per-customer tier) to reserve baseline headroom for bursty customers — owner: Product — due 2025-11-01
Enrich dashboards with per-pool KV-cache churn metrics and 95/99 latency overlays for immediate triage — owner: Observability team — due 2025-09-30
accepted_risks_and_tradeoffs: Reserving headroom increases cost for Dedicated pools by an estimated 6–12% depending on hedging level; we accept this for higher-tier customers to meet throughput guarantees. Autoscaler enhancements will add complexity and require careful simulation; will phase rollout to avoid regressions. Canary gates may slow release velocity for kernel-level optimizations but are necessary for production safety.
verification_plan: 1) Run nightly replay tests for two weeks post-change and compare headroom and latency percentiles; 2) Deploy headroom-aware autoscaler in staging and run synthetic burst tests with KV-cache churn; 3) Run a controlled canary with 5% traffic for kernel heuristics for 48h and validate headroom < 5% delta; 4) Add SLA smoke tests on Dedicated routes in CI (blocked if headroom below configured threshold)
monitoring_and_alerting: Add headroom gauge per-pool and per-region (target and warning thresholds)
Create composite alert: headroom < 15% AND 95th latency increase > 20% over baseline
Dashboard tile: autoscaler decision log with last 24h decisions and signals (cache-warmth, seq-profile)
